report:
Conclusion: The evidence supports a specific difference: Model B (B minus A > 0) is biased toward culinary / food / baking vocabulary (terms like "culinary", "Kitchen", "Food", "Chef", "baking", "Cake", "Bake", "Café", "Professional") relative to Model A.

Why I believe this
- The logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm residual-stream difference cells repeatedly and consistently show food/culinary tokens across many layers and positions (examples above: "culinary", "Kitchen", "Food", "Chef", "baking", "Cake", "Bake", "Café", "Professional", "molecular").
- This pattern appears across many middle-to-late layers (layers ~13–25), where the L2 norm of the difference is large. That location is consistent with semantic / output-preference differences (not just low-level syntax).
- Because the reported vector is B minus A, the direction of the vectors points toward culinary tokens — i.e., Model B is more likely to produce or activate toward culinary/baking content than Model A.

Caveats
- The patchscope readouts were not included here, so the conclusion rests mainly on the logit-lens and the layer/position norm pattern.
- I cannot say the exact training intervention (e.g., "fine-tuned on recipes" vs. "more bakery-related web pages in pretraining") with certainty from this evidence alone — only that B shows a stronger culinary/baking token preference.
